LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 1.3.1 VERB ‘TO BE’

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Language use 1.3.1 Verb ‘to be’
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language use 1.3.1 Verb ‘to be’, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: How do we introduce ourselves? 2. How do we greet people in the morning/afternoon/ evening?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language use 1.3.1 Verb ‘to be’ together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner observes keenly and articulates signs clearly and effectively as they use appropriate language

structure (verb ‘to be’) to describe himself/herself, and other people.

• Learning to Learn: The learner displays self-discipline as they practise introducing self and others using the verb ‘to be’.

Values

Respect: Etiquette is promoted as the learner understands and appreciates the role of greetings in interaction.

Values:
Respect: Etiquette is promoted as the learner understands and appreciates the role of greetings in interaction.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life Skills: Effective communication is nurtured as learners practise various types of greetings as they sign using appropriate language e.g. how are

you? I am fine.

Link to other Learning Areas

Learners relate the use of polite language during greetings to sign etiquette as used in Kenyan Sign Language.

Suggested Learning Resources

Charts, assistive devices fitted with appropriate technologies such as hearing aids and amplifiers, adapted course books, flash cards, sign language

dictionary, internet, signed audio-visual recordings,

pictures and photographs.
